tools_used: CourtListener MCP (docket search, docket-entries endpoint, opinion search)
web search and web fetch (supremecourt.gov docket, SCOTUSblog, Brennan Center tracker, the opposition PDF)
helpful: CourtListener docket-entries endpoint returned the full text of the D.C. Circuit's stay-denial order and the dissent in one call
The provisioned application text, which carries the whole procedural history
The statpack's interim section with per-Term counts, which made the pooled baseline a two-line computation
gaps: The respondents' opposition was filed before the snapshot date but was not provisioned; I had to fetch the PDF and extract its text myself (pypdf), which the fetch tool could not do
fedcourts query cannot filter to substantive applications only or to a government applicant, so its ranked rows were dominated by same-day time-extension grants and were useless as priors here
No conditioned interim cut exists for a federal-government applicant or for the response-requested rung; the pooled baseline is a different population from this cell
notes: Roughly 21 retrieval calls in total. The corpus service's first query cost 27 ranged GETs; the second was served warm.
